content.text: {"questions":[{"question_id":"Q1","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV059","EV011","EV061","EV013","EV063","EV035"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV016","EV018"],"status":"supported","reason":"There is direct or near-direct system evidence that TEOA is used in Co/bpy-relevant CO2 photoreduction formulations and that donor identity or concentration and medium ratio can affect CO/H2 outcomes or CO evolution, with TEOA also explicitly described as multifunctional donor/proton-source and amine-CO2 interactant. Transferable methods provide actual observables for additive effects: EPR spin-trapping can distinguish donor-derived radicals and transient absorption can report additive-dependent charge-carrier signals/lifetimes. Limits remain because no supplied source gives a strict head-to-head TEA versus TEOA comparison in one unchanged Co(II)-bipyridine formulation, but a plausible discriminating method exists."},{"question_id":"Q2","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV059","EV027","EV048","EV047","EV085","EV051"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV052","EV076","EV004","EV088"],"status":"partial","reason":"The supplied literature supports that catalyst identity, coordination environment, intermolecular interactions, and degradation can matter in cobalt or related photocatalytic CO2-reduction systems, and there is direct formulation evidence for CoCl2+bpy+TEOA platforms. However, direct evidence that TEA versus TEOA changes Co-bipyridine speciation or stability in the target family is not supplied. Usable characterization methods are available with explicit observables and limits: operando/in situ XAS/EXAFS can track coordination numbers, distances, and dynamic cobalt state, while operando approaches distinguish operating-state changes from before/after artifacts. Because mechanism support is indirect for the specific TEA/TEOA comparison, this family is only partial."},{"question_id":"Q3","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV053","EV007","EV065","EV041","EV011","EV095"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV053","EV018","EV005","EV077"],"status":"supported","reason":"This family has strong transferable mechanistic support that sacrificial donors can control reductive quenching, reduced-intermediate formation/lifetime, and downstream productive turnover in molecular photocatalysis, plus direct cobalt-system evidence for quenching analysis in TEOA-containing CO2 photoreduction. It also has concrete discriminating methods with observables: fluorescence/UV-vis quenching can distinguish donor-versus-catalyst quenching routes, transient absorption can monitor reduced-species or electron lifetimes, and luminescence quenching can report photoinduced electron transfer. Direct TEA versus TEOA evidence in Co-bpy is still absent, but both the question support and a plausible discriminating method are present."},{"question_id":"Q4","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV029","EV031","EV021","EV024"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV080","EV068"],"status":"partial","reason":"There is transferable evidence that donor environment can alter CO2 trapping or intermediate stability and that TEOA-specific chemistry may couple to substrate handling, but direct substrate-binding or intermediate-assignment evidence in a Co(II)-bipyridine TEA/TEOA system is not supplied. Method support is real but generic: operando FTIR/Raman/EPR and isotope-substitution controls can test vibrational assignments and distinguish hydrogen-containing adsorbates or binding states, yet no supplied source demonstrates a target-like Co-bpy substrate-assignment measurement under TEA/TEOA variation. Therefore the family is mechanistically suggestive with usable methods, but not sufficiently direct for supported."},{"question_id":"Q5","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV059","EV021","EV046","EV081","EV045","EV069"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV046","EV081","EV082"],"status":"supported","reason":"Performance and assay logic are well supported. Direct and transferable system evidence covers CO/H2 quantification, catalyst-omission/background contributions, dark/no-CO2 controls, donor-associated confounding, and 13CO2 origin checks. The methods are explicit and discriminating: GC quantifies CO and H2, GC-MS with 13CO2 tests carbon origin, and before/after characterization checks stability limits. Although the exact TEA-versus-TEOA effect in one Co-bpy formulation remains unconfirmed, this family has both evidence for the scientific question and clear usable methods for discrimination."},{"question_id":"Q6","mechanism_evidence_ids":["EV061","EV029","EV013","EV024","EV091","EV025"],"method_evidence_ids":["EV080"],"status":"partial","reason":"The literature provides several competing explanations beyond simple electron donation: proton-source behavior, amine-CO2 interaction, coordination or medium effects, and donor-side radical chemistry. But direct evidence in a Co(II)-bipyridine TEA/TEOA system that independently separates electron supply from these other roles is weak. Method evidence is also sparse: isotope-substitution/operando assignment logic is transferable, but no supplied source gives a well-established decoupling protocol with explicit observables for separating electron donation from protonation, coordination, and medium effects in the target class. Hence this family remains partial and relatively weak."}],"supplement_queries":[{"id":"SQ1","question_id":"Q6","channel":"teoa_system","question":"What studies on TEOA in photocatalytic CO2 reduction explicitly separate electron donation from proton, coordination, or medium effects in cobalt bipyridine or closely related molecular systems?","term_groups":[["TEOA","triethanolamine"],["cobalt","bipyridine","molecular"],["proton","coordination","viscosity"]]},{"id":"SQ2","question_id":"Q6","channel":"method","question":"Which methods can independently decouple electron transfer from proton management and coordination effects in additive dependent photocatalytic systems?","term_groups":[["isotope","titration","quenching"],["electron","proton","coordination"]]},{"id":"SQ3","question_id":"Q4","channel":"teoa_system","question":"What TEOA containing photocatalytic CO2 reduction studies identify cobalt or bipyridine bound CO2 adducts or downstream intermediates with assignable signals?","term_groups":[["TEOA","triethanolamine"],["cobalt","bipyridine"],["adduct","intermediate","assignment"]]},{"id":"SQ4","question_id":"Q4","channel":"method","question":"Which operando methods best assign CO2 binding and hydrogenated intermediates in molecular photocatalytic systems under additive variation?","term_groups":[["operando","ftir","raman","epr"],["binding","intermediate","isotope"]]},{"id":"SQ5","question_id":"Q2","channel":"teoa_system","question":"Are TEA and TEOA reported to change cobalt bipyridine speciation or stability during photocatalytic CO2 reduction under otherwise matched conditions?","term_groups":[["TEOA","triethanolamine"],["TEA","triethylamine"],["speciation","stability","degradation"]]},{"id":"SQ6","question_id":"Q2","channel":"method","question":"Which solution phase methods can resolve cobalt bipyridine speciation and degradation during illuminated CO2 reduction?","term_groups":[["uvvis","xas","epr","nmr"],["speciation","degradation","illumination"]]}]}
